header: This replaces the flat `mode: "surname"|"firstname"|"anyword"|"contains"|"auto"` + `excludePositions` scheme (29 Sep 2026). I made it genuinely compositional: a small, FIXED set of primitive checks, combined via AND/OR/NOT. This is my actual fix for the "still patchwork" problem raised in chat: a flat enum needs a new field/value every time a new LOGICAL COMBINATION shows up (which is unbounded), whereas composition via AND/OR/NOT is recursive and covers any combination of the EXISTING primitives for free. Only a genuinely new PRIMITIVE (a new kind of atomic check the backend can't already express) should ever make you touch this file again; combining existing primitives never should.

symbols.name: exactPhrasePattern
symbols.sig: function exactPhrasePattern(value: string): string
doc: I build the regex fragment for a literal word/phrase this way: each word escaped, joined by \s+ so a multi-word quoted phrase tolerates irregular spacing. BOTH the SQL compiler and the JS verifier use it, so exact matching is identical on each side by construction (same pattern, same case-insensitivity).

symbols.name: singleValue
symbols.sig: export function singleValue(pred: NamePredicate): string | null
doc: True when every leaf in the tree references the same single value, the common case (a query is "about" one name). I need this so the learned- pattern cache can safely substitute one {name} placeholder throughout the whole tree. I deliberately do NOT cache trees that reference more than one distinct value (see queryOrchestrator.ts): it is safer to re-run the LLM than to risk substituting the wrong value into the wrong leaf.

symbols.name: substituteValue
symbols.sig: export function substituteValue(pred: NamePredicate, to: string): NamePredicate
doc: Replaces every leaf's value with `to` and keeps the tree structure. I use it both to build a cacheable template (value -> "{name}") and to fill a matched template back in (the "{name}" placeholder -> a real value).

symbols.name: compileNamePredicate
symbols.sig: export function compileNamePredicate(pred: NamePredicate, params: any[]): string
doc: Compiles a NamePredicate into a parameterized SQL boolean expression. `params` is mutated (pushed to) as the source of truth for $N positions, matching the calling convention already used throughout rosterQuery.ts. It assumes the query already has `er` (employee_roster) and `u` (public."user", for name_phonetic) in scope/joined.

symbols.name: evaluateNamePredicate
symbols.sig: export function evaluateNamePredicate(pred: NamePredicate, name: string, phoneticCodes: string[] | null): boolean
doc: Evaluates a NamePredicate against one real employee's name (and their precomputed phonetic code array, if available). This is my independent, mechanical verification gate. It returns false (never throws) for a primitive type it doesn't recognize, so an unrecognized/future predicate type fails CLOSED (excludes the row) rather than silently passing everything through unchecked.
